subject: Post-demo: TTFT targets, burst & streaming pilot coordination
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@pivotalpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: TTFT targets, burst & streaming pilot coordination

Hi Elaine — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on TTFT and streaming behavior for the pilot with PivotalPay.

Recap (what we heard today)
- Primary goal: serve conversational fraud alerts and short-format transaction summaries to end users inside merchant apps. Typical responses are 40–120 tokens.
- Performance targets you called out: TTFT <= 200 ms for 90% of requests under normal load; occasional burst tolerance to 300–400 concurrent in flash scenarios.
- Preferred streaming: you prefer WebSocket for the demo because you want two-way control events; SSE is acceptable as fallback.

Proposed pilot scope (Redwood-drafted)
1) TTFT target: 150–200 ms median; 90th percentile target 300 ms (for payloads <= 120 tokens).
2) Concurrency & burst: steady concurrency target 50 qps with pilot pod sized for 200 steady qps; burst runway to 350 concurrent for 30s windows with graceful backpressure.
3) Streaming: WebSocket as primary (bi-directional), streaming chunks ~80–150 token cadence with first-chunk emit within TTFT target. Fallback to SSE where WS not supported.
4) Throughput: pilot loadgen plan will exercise 200 req/s sustained for 10 minutes, then run two burst windows (60s, 300 qps).

What we need from PivotalPay to start the pilot
- Representative sample payloads and token distribution (short, medium, long).
- A staging endpoint or list of client environments to test connectivity (mobile SDK versions, proxies/NAT behavior).
- Any security/network constraints (outbound port restrictions, TLS interception).

Next steps
- Can you share sample payloads and a staging contact by EOD Wednesday (May 4)?
- We’ll generate a small probe (attached format) to validate TTFT on our infra and share the ttft_probe_results.csv.
- Proposed pilot kickoff: May 10–11 (test windows + joint runbook).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.pdf (draft), pilot-pod-config.yaml (initial pod sizing).

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

---
From: Elaine Park <elaine@pivotalpay.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@pivotalpay.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT targets, burst & streaming pilot coordination

Thanks, Mateo — solid summary and appreciation for the suggested SLAs. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Payloads: primary events are 30–80 tokens (fraud alerts) and occasional 300+ token summaries for dispute context. I attached a small sample set (see inline).
- Network: mobile SDKs will be behind carrier NATs; some enterprise customers still proxy outbound traffic through port 443 only.
- Bursts: our busiest storefronts can spike to ~500 concurrent for <45s during peak promotions; we’re comfortable with Redwood exercising 350 for the pilot if you can show graceful degradation above that.

We can share a staging URL and an ops contact (ops@pivotalpay.com) by EOD Tuesday, May 4.

Happy to proceed with WebSocket as primary. Also please include guidance on chunk-cadence vs perceived UX when the client is rendering tokens live (we care a lot about the first visible token).

— Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Integrations, PivotalPay
elaine@pivotalpay.com

Date: 2027-05-03T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT targets, burst & streaming pilot coordination

Appreciate the details, Elaine — that maps to what we expected. Two quick notes:

1) UX / first visible token: from ops experience, sending a small initial chunk (4–12 tokens) immediately and then following with larger 80–120 token chunks gives a strong perceived TTFT while keeping kernel efficiency. We’ll include a small client-side example you can drop into the app.
2) Burst plan: for the pilot we’ll size a dedicated pod that can sustain 200 steady qps with automated short-term autoscaling to 350 qps (30–60s windows). If we see a real-world spike to 500 qps we will route to degraded-mode models (smaller quantized variants) before rejecting.

Proposed schedule:
- May 4: PivotalPay provides sample payloads + staging contact.
- May 6: Redwood runs internal probe and shares ttft_probe_results.csv.
- May 10: Joint pilot kickoff, 2-hour window to run steady + burst tests.

Do these dates work for you? If yes we’ll lock resources.

Thanks — Mateo

Mateo — prepping the pilot infra. Quick operational notes and ask: 

- I’ve drafted a pilot pod config (pilot-pod-config.yaml) that mirrors 2x T4s equivalent with KV cache priming to optimize short-response TTFT. Config attached.
- I’ll need approval to allocate a temporary dedicated pool on May 10–11. Estimated cost: ~3 days of reserved capacity; I’ll get precise numbers after we confirm the exact test windows.
- For loadgen: please confirm which tokenization scheme you’ll use for the probe (we need to match your client sample).

If you approve I’ll spin up the pod May 8 in our staging region (us-west1) and run a dry probe May 9. I’ll push the ttft_probe_results.csv afterward.

— Irene

Thanks all — quick confirmations before we kick off next week: 

- PivotalPay: confirmed sample payloads received and staging contact (ops@pivotalpay.com) — thanks, Elaine.
- Infra: Irene will spin up pilot pod in us-west1 on May 8 (dry run May 9).
- Probe: we’ll run the 200 qps steady test plus two burst windows (60s @ 300 qps, 45s @ 350 qps). If those pass, we’ll attempt one controlled 500 qps spike to validate graceful fallback.
- Streaming cadence: default first-chunk small (8 tokens), then 100-token batches; we’ll test trade-offs in perceived latency vs tokenization overhead and share a short client snippet.

Deliverables timeline
- May 9: ttft_probe_results.csv (Redwood internal probe)
- May 10: Joint pilot kickoff (2-hour window) + mutual-action-plan.pdf signed off

Attachments included: ttft_probe_results.csv (after dry run), pilot-pod-config.yaml, mutual-action-plan.pdf (final draft).

Elaine — please confirm you’re still good for May 10 and whether ops@pivotalpay.com needs an invite for the kickoff window.

Best — Mateo
